questions: Does "parity" refer to the number of digits in the palindrome (even/odd digit-length) or the parity of the palindrome's numeric value?
Are single-digit numbers (1-9) considered palindromes, and if so, are they odd-length?
What is the exact order of the two counts in the returned tuple — (even count, odd count) or the reverse?
Is the range "range(1, n)" meant literally as Python's range semantics (excluding n) despite the text saying "inclusive"?
Should n = 1 result in an empty range, or include just the value 1?
Are negative numbers or zero ever part of the range being considered, given "positive integer n"?
Does a palindrome need more than one digit to count, or is a single digit trivially a palindrome?
Should leading zeros be considered when checking palindrome status?
answers: Parity refers to the numeric value being even or odd, not the digit-length.
Single-digit numbers are considered palindromes, and their parity is based on their numeric value, not digit-length.
The order is (even count, odd count).
The range is inclusive of n, so it's from 1 to n inclusive, not Python's exclusive range.
n = 1 includes just the value 1, resulting in (0, 1).
No, the range is from 1 to n inclusive, so negative numbers and zero are not considered.
Single-digit numbers are trivially palindromes and count.
No, leading zeros are not considered; palindrome status is checked on the standard decimal representation without leading zeros.
